subject: StreamLatch: Processor Roster + Controlled Transit Paths (audit packet request)
messages:
From: Lucie Martin <lucie@streamlatch.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: IT Procurement <procure@streamlatch.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: StreamLatch pilot — need full processor roster + routing map

Hi Rachel,

We're getting ready to kick off the StreamLatch EU pilot next month and our security team is requesting a full subprocessor roster and a controlled-transit (onshore/egress) routing matrix for any services that touch EU customer data. Specifically, they asked for: 

- A flattened list of subprocessors (name, country of processing, role, contract start date)
- Which subprocessors have access to logs/telemetry vs. content tokens
- Any third-party transit paths that cross non-EU jurisdictions (and whether those are covered by SCCs or other mechanisms)
- A diagram or map showing where data can be routed and onshore fallback options

Can you share the packet by EOD Thursday? We need to get this into the procurement/audit review for the pilot. If you have a SOC2 report or any attestation PDFs that match the processors in question, please attach or point us to the drive link.

Thanks — Lucie
Lucie Martin
Head of IT Security, StreamLatch

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Lucie Martin <lucie@streamlatch.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StreamLatch pilot — need full processor roster + routing map

Hi Lucie — thanks for the heads up. Happy to run point on this.

Quick plan:
1) I'll pull together the current subprocessor roster and a dataflow map focused on EU ingress/egress.
2) Marissa will attach the inventory spreadsheet and note which partners touch logs vs. content.
3) Kimberly will confirm which processors are covered by SCCs, KMS boundaries, and whether we have onshore fallback lanes for EU customers.

We typically provide a compact audit packet (roster XLSX + dataflow PDF + links to SOC2 and KMS attestations). I can get a preliminary packet to you by Thursday EOD; if procurement needs more formal evidence (signed attestation, timeboxed export logs) we'll escalate to Legal.

A few clarifying Qs:
- Is the pilot limited to the EU27 only, or do you have cross-border pilot users (UK, CH)?
- Do you need token-level examples or just categorical access (logs vs content)?

I'll circulate the first draft once Marissa uploads the attachments.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Manager, Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi all — attaching the inventory we've been maintaining for EU customers. Notes below; full roster is in the XLSX (attached).

Attachment stubs:
- subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx (columns: processor_name | role | country | access_scope | contract_effective | scc_applied)
- streamlatch_dataflow_map.pdf (diagram: EU ingress --> regional routing --> optional onshore fallback)

Key callouts (high level):
- Telemetry/logs-only processors: LogStream (IE), MetricsBay (DE) — do not receive content tokens.
- Content-affecting processors: ModelHost EU (FR), CacheFast (IE) — these handle tokenized request/response. ModelHost EU is currently covered by SCC + customer-binding DPA addendum.
- Transits: Requests can be proxied through our edge fleet (IE, FR) and fall back to onshore-only pools (FR) if regional capacity is constrained. Non-EU transit (US-east) is only used as a last-resort failover and is protected via SCCs plus time-limited keystone tokens; we'll include the list of services that may touch data during failover.

I'll upload the two files to the Drive link Rachel noted and place a short README in the folder with SOC2 references.

— Marissa
Director, Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A couple of actionable items before we send the packet to StreamLatch procurement: 

- Legal needs the contract effective dates populated for the three processors handling content tokens (ModelHost EU, CacheFast, EdgeCache FR) and the current SCC template version applied. Please update the XLSX by tomorrow morning.
- Provide the SOC2 certificate/attestation links for ModelHost EU and LogStream; if we don't hold a copy, ask the vendor to provide time-limited access to their attestation.
- For any processors that perform key management (KMS/HSM), confirm whether keys are customer-specific or shared across tenants. That affects our recommended onshore fallback behavior.

Once those fields are in the roster I'll zip the packet and hand it to Legal for a short-form attestation letter they can attach to the DocuSign packet.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
